description:
Recorded with the original claim CORRECTED -- the /tmp-exhaustion framing did not survive verification, but two smaller real defects did.

ORIGINAL CLAIM: cfmesh's polyMesh round-trip test resolves its temp dir from the system temp dir and fails on a small or full /tmp -- an Android/Termux hazard.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (verified 2026-08-07):
- Location confirmed: crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/foam.rs:171, in test write_polymesh_disk_round_trip (:167-178):
      let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("cfmesh_polymesh_rt_{}", std::process::id()));
- BUT the data written is trivial. The mesh is cartesian_box(..., [2,2,2]) (:170) -- 8 cells, 12 internal + 24 boundary faces, 27 points (asserted :174-175). The written polyMesh is a few kilobytes. "Fails on a small /tmp" does not hold; only a completely full or unwritable temp dir would fail it.
- AND it is not hardcoded to /tmp. std::env::temp_dir() on Unix honours $TMPDIR, falling back to /tmp. Termux sets TMPDIR to its own prefix tmp, so on-device this resolves to Termux's writable temp. (Not verified on an actual device.)

TWO REAL DEFECTS THAT REMAIN:
1. A genuinely hardcoded /tmp exists ELSEWHERE: crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/examples/mesh_studio/main.rs:130
       export_dir: "/tmp/mesh_studio/polyMesh".into(),
   That one ignores $TMPDIR and would be wrong on Termux. (The example is Android-gated at :32-49, so it does not break the build -- but the path is still wrong for any non-/tmp TMPDIR, including some CI sandboxes.) Fix: use std::env::temp_dir().
2. Cleanup leak: foam.rs:177 `let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);` sits AFTER the assertions at :174-176, so a failing assertion leaks the directory. Fix: scope-guard the cleanup.

Note also that foam.rs has no target_os = "android" gate anywhere in src/ (only #[cfg(test)] at :103); the crate's only Android gates are Cargo.toml:36 (dev-deps) and examples/mesh_studio/main.rs:32/35/49. That is fine for this test as written, but worth knowing.
title: cfmesh: hardcoded /tmp in mesh_studio example + temp-dir cleanup leak (claim corrected)

description: Maintainer UI feedback on the graph/table digitiser, given interactively (not a GitHub comment this time). Six items: (1) project root should auto-open from the active paper/KovanRoot rather than the digitiser's own separate manual project_root/project_markdown_rel fields (op-96am legacy path, never updated when op-q1qj fixed this for the PDF reader's own annotations); (2) right-click 'Digitise graph'/'Read table' in the PDF reader should prompt for the figure identifier immediately (it currently crops and switches view with figure/page/document blank, no prompt); (3) page number and paper id/name should auto-populate from the already-open PDF/active paper instead of being asked (CropProvenance already carries page_index; DigitiseApp already has active_paper); (4) exported CSV: axis min/max should be recorded once, not per-row, and rows should contain only the actual digitised points -- reported as an actual bug in the exported file (not just perception), needs empirical verification since a static code read of to_csv_string() looked correct; (5) the 'operator' field is unclear -- rename to something self-explanatory and reduce friction (e.g. default from OS/git identity); (6) CSV/JSON export should use a native file picker rather than a typed path -- already done for the graph digitiser (op-jtna) but missing entirely from the table digitiser.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: All six items implemented: op-bd8p (auto project root from active paper, both digitisers), op-8ci2 (right-click Digitise-graph now prompts for the figure identifier before cropping), op-u1m9 (page/paper id/title auto-filled from CropProvenance/active_paper), op-xhay (CSV export stripped to bare x,y rows -- uncertainty and origin moved to JSON-only, per direct maintainer clarification during implementation, not the original static-code-read assumption), op-n0kz (operator field renamed to 'your name', pre-filled from OS login), op-jfc3 (table digitiser gained the same Browse... file-picker button the graph digitiser already had). All verified individually; cargo test -p kovan --lib --release: 383 passed, 0 failed as of the last child closed.

title: Digitiser UI dogfooding feedback (graph/table digitiser)

description: The item that blocks almost everything else in the MELCOR-lite epic. Given (P, U_pool, U_atm, M_H2O, M_NCG[i]) return temperatures, void fraction, partial pressures and the pool/atmosphere split, then invert to advance pressure. The gap is a STATE OBJECT plus wiring, not a missing solver (see the dwsim flash bead) -- but the pool/atmosphere NON-EQUILIBRIUM split (two separate energy equations, not one equilibrium state) still has to be built around a chemical-process flash. CVH, FL, HS condensation, RN condensation, BUR and SPR all call this.
title: melcor-cvh: two-phase pool+atmosphere control volume with N non-condensables

notes.content: Pure-algebra port DONE + V&V (34 tests) 2026-07-15: FsForcedConvectionHtc, PoolBoilingHtc (Shah/Gorenflo), FfForcedConvectionHtc, CHF/Leidenfrost/TONB/flow-enhancement/suppression/subcooled-boiling-fraction + multi-regime boiling in closures/heat_transfer/. description:
A gallery/dogfooding app in outram-park-digital-twin-engine that displays every visual component on one screen with live controls, so each widget can be built and quality-controlled ONE AT A TIME (maintainer's framing, 2026-08-03: 'construct widget by widget so there is some quality control').

SCOPE: gallery only. An authoring tool (compose a plant schematic interactively) is explicitly deferred to a future epic.

WHY: the components/ layer is far weaker than its bead history suggests. Inventory 2026-08-03 -- 1 genuine widget (PipeVisual, 281 lines, per-FV-cell colouring + tracers), 1 modest (ReactorVesselVisual), 4 single-rectangle colour-only (cooling tower, steam generator, turbine, valve), and 4 with NO state-derived detail at all (pump, condenser, heat exchanger, instrumentation -- flat circles/rects). op-wqk.3 is closed, but it delivered wrappers, not good widgets.

Corroborating symptom: op-wqk.9.4 records that htgr_sim_v1's schematic OMITS PipeVisual because standing up its fluid-array backend is disproportionate -- i.e. the one good widget is too awkward to use. A studio surfaces exactly this class of problem early.

DESIGN BAR (maintainer, 2026-08-03/04): a widget's look must derive from the real dimensions and design of the component -- turbine sizing, pipe bore and run -- not from arbitrary screen coordinates. Aesthetically: pipes connect smoothly, thickness reflects cross-sectional area, displayed length is proportional to real length, and angle follows elevation so natural-circulation loops read correctly. Avoid over-detailing; too much may confuse the end user.

CONSTRAINT: the engine crate forbids new physics (crate CLAUDE.md). Any missing dimension is added in tampines -- see op-dt3.17 and its children.
title: Widget Studio — gallery app for developing and QC-ing the visual component library
